description.en: Let people sign in to Casdoor with accounts on your own GitLab over OpenID Connect: the provider settings, and the OAuth application to create in GitLab.
The address of your GitLab instance, without a trailing slash.

guide.json.title: Self-Managed GitLab as a Sign-in Provider for Casdoor
guide.json.headline: Sign in to Casdoor with your own GitLab
guide.json.summary: GitLab is also an OpenID Connect provider. Casdoor's built-in GitLab provider only talks to gitlab.com; this template points Casdoor at your own GitLab, so developers sign in with the account they already use every day.

steps.title: Create an OAuth application in GitLab
steps.text: As an administrator, open **Admin → Applications** and click **Add new application**. (A group's **Settings → Applications** or your own **Edit profile → Applications** work too, without the Trusted option.) Fill in:

fields.label: Trusted
fields.value: On, to skip the consent screen

steps.title: Copy the credentials
steps.text: Save the application and copy the **Application ID** (the client ID) and the **Secret**. GitLab stores the secret hashed, so this is the only time you can see it.

tips: GitLab only sends `email` for users who have a public email address. Others arrive in Casdoor without an email.
Renewing the secret in GitLab breaks sign-in until you put the new one in Casdoor.

faqs.question: Does this work with gitlab.com?
faqs.answer: Yes, with `https://gitlab.com` as the GitLab URL, but Casdoor's built-in GitLab provider already covers gitlab.com.

faqs.question: Do GitLab groups come over?
faqs.answer: No. GitLab returns the user's groups from its userinfo endpoint, but Casdoor only fills in the standard profile from it, not Casdoor groups.
